title: Austria lowers the national basic digital skills target
period: Original and revised roadmap versions; 2025 progress reported in 2026
summary: Austria’s original roadmap uses a maximum-100% formulation and also contains a generic 80% heading. The Commission’s 2024 assessment identifies the national target as 100%. The revised roadmap sets 80% for 2030, supporting a 20-percentage-point reduction with the original qualifier retained.
facts: Original national target: 100% for 2030; original “max.” qualifier | Revised national target: 80% for 2030 | 2025 observed progress: 69.8% | Distance to revised target: 10.2 percentage points
notes: The 2024 Commission assessment resolves the national-versus-generic target ambiguity for this comparison. The measure covers people aged 16–74 with at least basic digital skills. The 2030 deadline is still ahead; no final delivery verdict or motive is inferred.

title: Finland raises its SME digital intensity target
period: Original and revised roadmap versions; 2025 progress reported in 2026
summary: Finland’s revised roadmap explicitly raises the 2030 target for SMEs with at least basic digital intensity from 90% to 95%. The 2025 DIIv3 result is 94.0%, one percentage point below the revised target.
facts: Original target: At least 90% by 2030 | Revised target: 95% by 2030 | 2025 DIIv3 observation: 94.0% | Revision version and memo date: December 2024 version; 15 January 2025 memo
notes: The surveyed SME group has 10–249 workers. Earlier DII baselines use a different version, so the 94.0% figure does not establish fulfillment of the original commitment. A pre-deadline distance is not a final 2030 verdict.

title: Estonia adds national KPI targets; an old percentage is not a baseline
period: Original and revised roadmap versions; 2025 progress reported in 2026
summary: The 2026 Commission report identifies 13 new national targets in Estonia’s 2025 roadmap. The older skills objective of 60% concerns above-basic skills by 2035; the new 80% concerns at least basic skills by 2030. They cannot be treated as a 20-point increase or a five-year acceleration. The revised roadmap also supplies a national cloud-adoption target.
facts: New national targets reported: 13 | Older skills objective: 60%; above-basic skills; 2035 | New skills target: 80%; at least basic skills; 2030 | New national cloud target: 75% by 2030
notes: Added means newly specified national KPIs in the selected roadmap comparison, not the country’s first related policy promises. EU collective targets and annual planned trajectories are not national observed results.

title: Finland adds an FTTP target beside its VHCN target
period: Original and revised roadmap versions; 2025 progress reported in 2026
summary: Finland explicitly adds a 100% FTTP coverage target for 2030 in the revised roadmap. Its 2025 FTTP coverage is 80.0%, while VHCN coverage is 84.6%. The two indicators describe different network coverage measures and remain separate.
facts: New FTTP target: 100% by 2030 | 2025 FTTP coverage: 80.0% | 2025 VHCN coverage: 84.6% | Revised VHCN target: 100% by 2030
notes: Coverage concerns households, not the proportion subscribing to fibre. An added FTTP target does not mean earlier network policy was absent. The original broad gigabit narrative also mentions enterprises, so it is not assessed as fulfilled using the narrower household observation.

title: The same 75% can refer to a different indicator
period: Original and revised roadmap versions; 2025 progress reported in 2026
summary: The original target table specifies 75% for big-data adoption; the revised table specifies 75% for data analytics. The indicator and measurement scope changed, so equal numbers cannot establish an unchanged target on the same definition.
facts: Original target label: Big data; 75% by 2030 | Revised target label: Data analytics; 75% by 2030 | 2025 data analytics observation: 45.1% | Cross-version comparison: Held
notes: Official methodology states that data analytics covers a broader technology set. The original narrative says SMEs while its table says enterprises, which is another retained ambiguity. No old-target gap or policy-strengthening/weakening conclusion is calculated.

title: Estonia’s edge-node target remains unresolved
period: Original and revised roadmap versions; 2025 progress reported in 2026
summary: The 2026 summary table lists an Estonian edge-node target of 5, but the report narrative says no target was set and the 2025 roadmap’s national-target cell is a dash. The 2025 estimate of 28 nodes uses a new method. Both the target and cross-version outcome comparison remain held.
facts: Roadmap national target: Dash; no numeric target | 2026 report summary target: 5 | 2026 report narrative: No national target set | 2025 estimate: 28 nodes; new methodology
notes: The 10,000 figure in the roadmap is the EU target, not Estonia’s. Neither 28 divided by 5 nor growth from the earlier baseline is reported. The conflicting sources need clarification; no final delivery conclusion is made.
